evidence.title: Barranco León & Fuente Nueva-3 (Orce, Guadix-Baza Basin, Spain): 1.4 Ma earliest Europeans
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, magnetostratigraphy and micro-mammal biostratigraphy bracketing a deciduous molar (BL02-J54-100), limestone choppers and butchered hippo/mammoth carcasses.
evidence.summary: Preserves the oldest widely accepted hominin deciduous molar and Oldowan-mode flint/limestone lakeside assemblages in Western Europe.
evidence.limits: A single worn milk tooth resists fine distinction between Eurasian early Homo and Homo antecessor.

evidence.title: Sima del Elefante TE7–TE9 (Atapuerca, Spain): 1.4–1.1 Ma ATE7-1 mid-face & mandible
evidence.dateBasis: 26Al/10Be cosmogenic nuclide burial ages, palaeomagnetism and microfauna across lower karst levels TE7 and TE9.
evidence.summary: Revealed both the 1.2–1.1 Ma ATE9-1 mandible and the deeper 1.4–1.1 Ma ATE7-1 mid-facial skeleton (“Homo affinis erectus”), proving an earlier pre-antecessor Iberian settlement phase.
evidence.limits: Deep karst breccia infill preserves partial fragmented facial elements rather than complete crania.

evidence.title: Pirro Nord (Gargano, Italy) & Kozarnika Cave (Bulgaria): 1.4–1.0 Ma SE/Mediterranean dispersal
evidence.dateBasis: Pre-Jaramillo Villafranchian biochronology and palaeomagnetic sequences across Italian karst fissures and Balkan cave entrance strata.
evidence.summary: Marks early Mode 1 core-and-flake expansion across Mediterranean and Danubian–Balkan gateways (including incised bones and flints at Kozarnika and flint cores at Pirro Nord) prior to northern European stabilization.
evidence.limits: Sparse tephra markers in early fissures produce wider confidence intervals (~1.4–1.1 Ma).

evidence.title: Happisburgh & Pakefield (East Anglia Coast, Britain): 950–680 ka northern estuary hominins
evidence.dateBasis: Reversed Cromerian-complex estuarine palaeomagnetism, pollen/coleoptera biozones and short-lived 2013 intertidal footprint laser scans.
evidence.summary: Contains the oldest direct hominin footprints outside Africa at ~950–850 ka on a boreal Thames–Bytham estuary flat, showing seasonal high-latitude persistence north of the Alps.
evidence.limits: Tidal wave erosion destroyed the exposed Happisburgh footprint horizon within weeks of laser-scanning.

evidence.title: Caune de l’Arago (Tautavel, France): “Tautavel Man” & 200-ka Middle Pleistocene hunting archive
evidence.dateBasis: Multimethod ESR/U-series and palaeoclimatic correlation across Arago Soil Complex layers (~450 ka Arago 21 skull up to 580 ka basal units).
evidence.summary: Preserves more than 150 Middle Pleistocene hominin elements—foremost the ~450 ka Arago 21 cranium—amid cold-steppe horse, mouflon and reindeer ambush horizons overlooking the Verdouble gorge.
evidence.limits: Long-term karst percolation complicates trace-element uranium modelling in deep floor breccia.

evidence.title: Boxgrove (West Sussex, Britain): ~480 ka Acheulean beach & Homo heidelbergensis tibia
evidence.dateBasis: Biostratigraphy (Mimomys–Arvicola vole clock) and chalk-cliff raised-marine silt correlation.
evidence.summary: Snap-frozen chalk-lagoon landscape preserving pristine knapping scatters from individual symmetrical ovate handaxes, butchered horse/rhino carcasses, antler soft hammers and a massive H. heidelbergensis shinbone.
evidence.limits: No genetic material survives from the MIS 13 marine silts to test affinity directly with Sima de los Huesos.

evidence.title: Gruta da Aroeira (Almonda Karst, Portugal): ~400 ka Aroeira 3 cranium & Acheulean bifaces
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-series dating of calcite flowstones sealing the Aroeira 3 cranium, handaxes and burnt animal bones.
evidence.summary: Connects western Iberian Atlantic Acheulean biface users anatomically with European Middle Pleistocene pre-Neanderthal populations while highlighting regional cranial mosaicism.
evidence.limits: Represents a single partial cranium lacking post-cranial skeleton in that chamber horizon.

evidence.title: Gran Dolina TD10 & Galería (Atapuerca, Spain): Communal bison hunting & Levallois shift
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, OSL and U-series chronologies across Gran Dolina TD10.1–TD10.4 Acheulean-to-Middle Paleolithic subunits.
evidence.summary: Subunit TD10.2 preserves mass-kill butchered Bison schoetensacki bonebeds evidencing coordinated seasonal hunting and early Middle Paleolithic centripetal/Levallois core reduction.
evidence.limits: Stratigraphic boundaries between late Mode 2 and early Mode 3 units reflect gradual local organizational change.

evidence.title: Schöningen (Lower Saxony, Germany): Complete wooden spears & cooperative horse hunting
evidence.dateBasis: Waterlogged lignite-mine lake-shore strata dated by amino-acid racemization (~200 ka) alongside classic ~300 ka MIS 9 correlations.
evidence.summary: Waterlogged organic preservation reveals carefully balanced spruce throwing spears, throwing sticks, antler tools and >50 butchered lakeshore wild horses documenting structured cooperative ambush.
evidence.limits: Ongoing geochronological debate centers on MIS 9 (~300 ka) versus MIS 7 (~200 ka) lake-basin assignment.

evidence.title: Apidima Cave (Mani Peninsula, Greece): ~210 ka & ~170 ka cranial mosaic in the Balkans
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-series dating and virtual 3D morphometric reconstruction of breccia-embedded Apidima 1 (~210 ka) and Apidima 2 (~170 ka) posterior crania.
evidence.summary: Raises the landmark hypothesis that an early out-of-Africa Homo sapiens dispersal reached southern Greece by ~210,000 years ago before subsequent replacement by late Middle Pleistocene Neanderthals.
evidence.limits: No stone tools accompany the sea-cliff breccia pocket, and some specialists caution that post-mortem distortion in Apidima 1 merits conservative species interpretation.

evidence.title: Bruniquel Cave & Baume Moula-Guercy (Southern France): Deep karst rings & cannibalized kin
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-series dating of 400 intentionally snapped stalagmites arranged in 176 ka subterranean rings at Bruniquel alongside Moula-Guercy Eemian fossil/cutmark sequences.
evidence.summary: Documents complex Early Neanderthal subterranean cave architecture built 336 metres from daylight at Bruniquel (176.5 ka), alongside Last Interglacial Rhone-corridor Neanderthal lifeways at Moula-Guercy.
evidence.limits: Deep cave isolation makes Bruniquel’s ritual versus technical purpose difficult to determine with certainty.

evidence.title: Krapina (Hušnjakovo Rock Shelter, Croatia): Last Interglacial >800 Neanderthal fossils
evidence.dateBasis: ESR and U-series dating of sandstone shelter deposits yielding >800 remains of dozens of Neanderthals and polished/cutmarks on white-tailed eagle talons.
evidence.summary: Forms Europe’s largest single-site Neanderthal skeletal sample (~130 ka), exhibiting healing injuries, stone-tool cutmarks and curated white-tailed sea eagle talons interpreted as personal ornaments.
evidence.limits: 1899–1905 Gorjanović-Kramberger stratigraphic records predate modern micro-taphonomic provenance mapping.

evidence.title: Gorham’s & Vanguard Caves (Gibraltar): Coastal Mediterranean Neanderthals & cliff engraving
evidence.dateBasis: OSL/radiocarbon chronologies of Mousterian coastal middens (monk seal, dolphin, Limpet shells), raptor-feather cutmarks and bedrock geometric hatchings.
evidence.summary: Sea-level coastal caves at the Strait of Gibraltar show Neanderthals harvesting coastal marine resources, capturing corvid/raptor wing feathers, distilling birch/rockrose tar in small hearths and incising cross-hatched bedrock lines.
evidence.limits: Late persistence debates (<32 ka) remain sensitive to subtle radiocarbon contamination filtering.

evidence.title: La Ferrassie, Le Moustier & La Chapelle-aux-Saints (SW France): Neanderthal burials & genetics
evidence.dateBasis: Stratigraphic/OSL re-excavations of Ferrassie pits alongside nuclear DNA and isolation bottlenecks traced in late Rhône/Aquitaine Neanderthal individuals.
evidence.summary: Classic Dordogne and Corrèze limestone shelters defined the Mousterian industry and supplied multiple articulated Neanderthal adult, child and infant burials while recent genomes reveal small, genetically isolated late communities.
evidence.limits: Early twentieth-century clearance removed most undisturbed context around several classic museum skeletons.

evidence.title: El Sidrón & Prado Vargas (Northern Spain): Kinship genetics, calculus medicine & fossil collecting
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient nuclear/mtDNA/dental-calculus genomics on 13 El Sidrón individuals alongside Mousterian Level 4 excavations at Prado Vargas.
evidence.summary: Reveals patrilocal small-band kinship (three closely related adult males paired with diverse females) at El Sidrón, medicinal plant poplar/camomile residues in plaque, and marine fossil curation by Neanderthals at Prado Vargas.
evidence.limits: El Sidrón represents a single secondary mud-flow bone accumulation rather than a multi-period occupation.

evidence.title: Vindija Cave (Croatia): High-coverage late Neanderthal reference genome
evidence.dateBasis: Hydroxyproline single-amino-acid AMS redating and 30x high-coverage nuclear genome assembly of specimen Vindija 33.19.
evidence.summary: Supplied the highest-precision genetic portrait of late European Neanderthals immediately prior to disappearance, clarifying shared ancestry (~50–45 ka) with the Neanderthals who admixed with incoming Homo sapiens.
evidence.limits: Cryoturbation inside karst G3/G1 boundaries mixes late Mousterian and early Upper Paleolithic split-base points unless bones are directly dated.

evidence.title: Spy, Goyet (Belgium) & Feldhofer (Germany): Northwestern late Neanderthal extinction window
evidence.dateLabel: c. 46,000–40,000 years ago (Neander Valley type site & Meuse)
evidence.dateBasis: Genomic diversity studies and compound-specific amino-acid radiocarbon dating across Meuse Valley Goyet/Spy and 1856 Feldhofer remains.
evidence.summary: Shows low genetic diversity and regional turnover among the final northwestern European Neanderthals around 44–40 ka cal BP, including selective female/juvenile cannibalism signatures at Goyet Troisième Caverne.
evidence.limits: Limited sample sizes constrain exact population-census estimates across northern river plains.

evidence.title: Grotte Mandrin (Rhône Valley, France): ~54 ka modern-human excursion between Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: Soot-layer fuliginochronology, OSL/radiocarbon and dental morphology connecting Layer E Neronian micro-points to an earlier H. sapiens tooth.
evidence.summary: Preserves a brief early Homo sapiens Neronian bow-and-arrow excursion ~54,000 years ago inside the Rhône corridor—within a year of preceding Neanderthals—before Neanderthals returned for another ~10 millennia.
evidence.limits: No nuclear DNA is yet published from the isolated Layer E Mandrin milk tooth to test genetic continuity.

evidence.title: Ilsenhöhle at Ranis (Germany) & Zlatý kůň (Czechia): High-latitude H. sapiens ~45 ka genomes
evidence.dateBasis: Proteomic ZooMS identification, direct bone AMS radiocarbon and whole-genome sequencing of 13 individuals spanning Ranis LRJ leaf-points and Zlatý kůň.
evidence.summary: Proves that pioneers of the cold north-central European steppe bearing Lincombian-Ranisian-Jerzmanowician leaf points by 45 ka were Homo sapiens genetically continuous with the Zlatý kůň basal Eurasian–European lineage.
evidence.limits: Small pioneering family band left few cultural traces across wide northern steppes before the Campanian Ignimbrite.

evidence.title: Grotta di Fumane & Grotta del Cavallo (Italy): Uluzzian & Protoaurignacian transitions
evidence.dateBasis: Campanian Ignimbrite (39.9 ka) volcanic tephra markers, shell-bead ornaments and deciduous tooth morphometrics at Cavallo beneath Protoaurignacian layers at Fumane.
evidence.summary: Charts rapid expansion across peninsular and pre-Alpine Italy by makers of crescentic Uluzzian backed blades, painted limestone slabs (Fumane) and perforated Mediterranean shell beads prior to the Campanian Ignimbrite ash.
evidence.limits: Debate persists in select Italian sequences over local Mousterian admixture vs sharp cultural turnover.

evidence.title: Kostenki–Borshchevo Complex (Middle Don, Russia): 40–20 ka steppe camps & Kostenki 14 genome
evidence.dateBasis: Campanian Ignimbrite tephra seals, Kostenki 14 (~38 ka) and Kostenki 18 child burial genomes across 26 open-air loess-terrace sites.
evidence.summary: Preserves Europe’s longest open-air Upper Paleolithic terrace record along the Don River, where Kostenki 14 already carries all core West Eurasian ancestral components alongside early ivory/limestone art and Gravettian child burials.
evidence.limits: Permafrost solifluction on river terraces displaces minor stone clusters along early Aurignacian–Streletskayan boundaries.

evidence.title: Swabian Jura Caves (Hohle Fels, Vogelherd & Stadel, Germany): 40 ka ivory art, flutes & signs
evidence.dateBasis: Ultrafiltration radiocarbon and ESR/U-series chronologies for Aurignacian figurative mammoth-ivory sculptures, swan/vulture/ivory flutes and geometric sign sequences.
evidence.summary: Yields the earliest dated figurative sculpture (~40 ka Hohle Fels Venus), the composite half-human half-lion Löwenmensch from Hohlenstein-Stadel, functioning multi-hole bone/ivory flutes and repeatable Aurignacian conventional signs.
evidence.limits: Early twentieth-century Vogelherd excavations disturbed exact sub-spits for several portable carvings.

evidence.title: Chauvet-Pont d’Arc Cave (Ardèche, France): ~36 ka Aurignacian monumental cave sanctuaries
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on Scots-pine torch soot, charcoal drawings and cave-bear floor bones sealed by rockfall ~21,500 BP.
evidence.summary: Preserves >400 Aurignacian and Gravettian wall compositions showcasing dynamic perspective herds of cave lions, wooly rhinoceroses, mammoths, bison and a bear skull placed on a central altar block.
evidence.limits: Strict preservation prevents destructive floor trenching across pristine wolf, bear and human footprints.

evidence.title: Dolní Věstonice & Pavlov (Moravia, Czechia): ~29 ka mammoth settlements, ceramic kilns & textiles
evidence.dateBasis: Extensive radiocarbon sequences across seasonal mammoth-hunting villages, high-temperature loess clay kilns (~26,000 BP ceramics) and the triple burial.
evidence.summary: Loess slopes in Moravia held semi-permanent Gravettian base camps featuring the world’s earliest known fired-clay animal and Venus statuettes, textile/basketry impressions on clay, musical rasps and elaborate multi-individual burials.
evidence.limits: Industrial clay quarrying destroyed portions of the southern Dolní Věstonice terrace in the early twentieth century.

evidence.title: Willendorf & Krems-Wachtberg (Wachau Danube, Austria): Venus of Willendorf & twin infant burial
evidence.dateBasis: Loess palaeosoil stratigraphy plus direct aDNA/radiocarbon (~31 ka cal BP) on Krems-Wachtberg monozygotic twins buried beneath a mammoth shoulder blade.
evidence.summary: Combines the red-ochre limestone Venus of Willendorf (materially sourced via micro-CT/petrography from northern Italy/Moravia) with Krems-Wachtberg’s deeply touching mammoth-ivory-beaded monozygotic twin newborn burial.
evidence.limits: Early 1908 Willendorf terrace trenching limits fine micro-provenience of associated hearths.

evidence.title: Sunghir (Klyazma Valley, Vladimir, Russia): ~32 ka royal-scale Gravettian ivory-bead burials
evidence.dateBasis: Hydroxyproline compound-specific AMS radiocarbon and whole-genome sequencing of Sunghir 1–4 burials.
evidence.summary: Sunghir 1 (adult man) and Sunghir 2–3 (two juveniles head-to-head) were interred on open Russian tundra-steppe draped in ~10,000 drilled mammoth-ivory beads, Arctic fox canines, disk carvings and 2-metre straightened mammoth-tusk spears.
evidence.limits: Open-air camp structures around the burials suffered severe late-glacial solifluction.

evidence.title: Arene Candide Cave (Liguria, Italy): Gravettian “Young Prince” & Epigravettian necropolis
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on “Il Principe” (~28 ka cal BP) and ~20 formal Younger Dryas Epigravettian ochre burials topped with elk/deer antler caches and pierced shells.
evidence.summary: Overlooking the Ligurian coast, Arene Candide preserves two world-renowned Paleolithic funerary horizons: the tall Gravettian adolescent crowned with hundreds of Cyclope neritea shells and flint blade (~28 ka) and a dense terminal Pleistocene necropolis.
evidence.limits: Historical excavations removed upper Bronze/Neolithic overburden while keeping deep Pleistocene cemetery corners.

evidence.title: Altamira, El Castillo & El Mirón (Cantabria, Spain): Earliest red disks, LGM “Red Lady” & bison halls
evidence.dateBasis: Uranium-series minimum calcite ages (>40.8 ka El Castillo disk) plus AMS/aDNA on Magdalenian El Mirón “Red Lady” and polychrome Altamira ceiling paintings.
evidence.summary: Cantabrian limestone galleries chronicle >25,000 years of parietal painting from >40.8 ka red spheres and hand stencils through Magdalenian polychrome bison ceilings at Altamira and ochre-covered female burials at El Mirón.
evidence.limits: Debate continues between pre-sapiens Neanderthal attribution vs earliest Aurignacian authorship of >40 ka calcite-capped motifs.

evidence.title: Côa Valley & Siega Verde (Douro Basin, Portugal/Spain): Open-air Ice Age river-cliff rock art
evidence.dateBasis: OSL/TL luminescence and radiocarbon dating of riverside Gravettian–Magdalenian schist-engraved habitation panels along the Côa and Águeda rivers.
evidence.summary: Demonstrates that Paleolithic rock art was not restricted to deep dark caves: thousands of finely pecked and incised overlapping horses, aurochs, ibex and red deer stretch across kilometres of sunlit schist river valleys.
evidence.limits: Exposed schist outcrops lack cave-calcite Uranium-series crusts, anchoring styles via excavated adjacent campsite floors.

evidence.title: Cueva del Malalmuerzo & Parpalló (Southern Iberia): LGM glacial refugium genetic link
evidence.dateBasis: Direct 23,000 cal BP genome of a Solutrean individual from Andalusia paired with Parpalló’s >5,000 engraved limestone plaquettes.
evidence.summary: Confirms southern Iberia as an Ice Age human refugium during maximum European ice-sheet expansion, revealing continuous genetic survival from pre-LGM Western Europeans into later post-glacial Magdalenian populations.
evidence.limits: Extreme LGM aridity left sparse open-air Solutrean camps across much of central inland Iberia.

evidence.title: Lascaux, La Madeleine & Abri Pataud (Vézère Valley, France): Magdalenian sanctuary & exchange
evidence.dateBasis: AMS antler/reindeer bone dates across Solutrean/Badegoulian/Magdalenian type shelters alongside Mediterranean-to-Atlantic shell and stone exchange.
evidence.summary: As glaciers receded, Southwestern France hosted the monumental Lascaux painted halls, delicately sculpted Magdalenian spear-throwers and harpoons (La Madeleine), and dense long-distance Mediterranean/Atlantic social networks.
evidence.limits: Historic conservation closures preserve Lascaux’s microbial equilibrium by restricting intrusive sub-floor digging.

evidence.title: Mezhyrich & Yudinovo (Dnieper–Desna Basin, Ukraine/Russia): Interlocking mammoth-bone dwellings
evidence.dateBasis: Revised ultrafiltration AMS radiocarbon dates on mammoth bone structural elements, storage pits and painted mammoth skulls.
evidence.summary: On treeless post-LGM periglacial river terraces, Epigravettian hunters engineered circular dwellings, storage pits and ritual middens from hundreds of interlocking mammoth skulls, mandibles, tusks and long bones.
evidence.limits: Re-used fossilized mammoth bones collected from nearby thawing ravines require multiple radiocarbon assays to isolate occupation spans.

evidence.title: Gönnersdorf (Rhine) & Petersfels (Germany): Slate-paved campsites & engraved plaquettes
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon-dated volcanic-pumice-sealed Rhine settlement floors yielding circular slate-slab pavements and >400 stylized engraved female/horse slate plaquettes.
evidence.summary: Documents rapid re-expansion into Central Europe during Bølling warming, leaving remarkably intact multi-season paved tipi floors, jet beads, horse/reindeer hunting camps and shared stylistic plaquette motifs from Iberia to the Rhine.
evidence.limits: Rapid Laacher See ~13 ka volcanic eruption buried and altered adjacent younger Federmesser camps.

evidence.title: Riparo Villabruna & Tagliente (Italian Pre-Alps): Earliest dental treatment & “Villabruna” ancestry
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on the ~14 ka cal BP Villabruna 1 skeleton, scanning-electron microscopy of chipped-flint dental scraping and genome-wide Villabruna/WHG turnover.
evidence.summary: Captures both the earliest documented flint-tool surgical treatment of a carious molar and the rise of the “Villabruna Cluster” Western Hunter-Gatherer ancestry that reshaped European populations after 14,000 BP.
evidence.limits: Montane limestone rockshelters sample southern Alpine corridors better than submerged Adriatic coastal plains.

evidence.title: Grotte du Bichon (Jura), Blätterhöhle & Stellmoor (N Europe): Azilian to Younger Dryas hunters
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dating on Azilian bear-hunter skeleton (Bichon ~13.7 ka cal BP), Federmesser woodland flint camps and Younger Dryas Ahrensburgian reindeer arrow shafts at Stellmoor.
evidence.summary: Traces woodland Azilian and Federmesser bow-and-arrow hunters alongside Younger Dryas Ahrensburgian tundra-edge reindeer hunters using pine arrow shafts across Doggerland–northern Germany to western Scotland.
evidence.limits: Inundation of Doggerland beneath the North Sea leaves terrestrial Late Glacial camp networks only partially mapped from dredging.

waves.title: Early & Middle Pleistocene Peopling of Southern and Northwestern Europe
waves.dateBasis: Links Kozarnika, Pirro Nord, Tautavel, Orce, Atapuerca, Boxgrove and Schöningen magnetostratigraphic and biostratigraphic anchors.
waves.summary: Schematic Mediterranean–Atlantic corridor showing pulsed glacial-interglacial colonization of southern and temperate Europe across nearly one million years.
waves.limits: Represents episodic interglacial expansions separated by severe northern European depopulations during extreme glaciations.

waves.title: Initial Upper Paleolithic & Aurignacian Expansion across Danube, Rhône and Northern Plains
waves.dateBasis: Connects Bacho Kiro, Oase, Willendorf/Krems, Ranis/Zlatý kůň, Swabian Jura, Chauvet and Cantabria genomic and AMS datasets.
waves.summary: Schematic Danubian and western corridor illustrating early Homo sapiens blade dispersals, regional Neanderthal admixture events and the explosion of Aurignacian figurative art and music.
waves.limits: Different genetic waves (Zlatý kůň/Ranis, Bacho Kiro and Aurignacian Goyet/Vogelherd) did not form one uniform lineage.

waves.title: Post-Glacial Magdalenian & Epigravettian Recolonization from Southern European Refugia
waves.dateBasis: Links Iberian/South French Magdalenian and Italian Villabruna/Epigravettian aDNA tracks re-populating central Europe, Britain and Doggerland.
waves.summary: Schematic post-Last Glacial Maximum northward recolonization paths tracking Magdalenian and Villabruna-cluster Western Hunter-Gatherer ancestry across warming valleys.
waves.limits: Submerged continental shelves across the English Channel, Adriatic and North Sea hide key lowland routes.
